title: Milestones on Simple Roadmap's Timeline and Gantt
subtitle: Add one or more milestones right on the chart, see them on the goal's ladder, and see a PRD's own milestones. Invented company and data.

decisions.name: How to add on the chart
decisions.question: How does the owner add one or more milestones right on the Timeline, Gantt and Now / Next / Later?
decisions.common: Everything stays in Simple. Every way ends in the same card (MS2) and draws the milestone on the Timeline, the Gantt and Now / Next / Later at once, with Undo.

proposals.name: Click the time axis
proposals.what: Pointing at the time axis shows a hollow diamond and “+ Milestone on <day>” that follow the pointer. A click drops it on that day and opens the card in the chart's top corner, in the goal whose rows are under it; bars tapped while the card is open become the items it waits on. “Add and place another” saves it and keeps the add going for the next click. On a phone a tap on the axis does the same and the card comes up as a sheet. Now / Next / Later gets a “+ Milestone” in each horizon.
proposals.plus: The day is picked by where you click, so no date typing; works the same on Timeline, Gantt and phone; several in a row without closing anything.
proposals.cost: A thin target on the axis; the pointer guide is new drawing to build and test on both charts.

frames.caption: At rest: Grow retention's ladder (M1 Nov 20, M2 Dec 22) and Faster activation's M1, each named in its goal's row; a faint “+ Milestone” sits on the time axis.
The pointer on the time axis at Jan 20: a hollow diamond and “+ Milestone on Jan 20, 2027” follow it, with a guide line down the chart.
Clicked: the card opens in the chart's top corner with Grow retention picked; the two bars tapped on the chart are outlined as its items, and one ends after it.
Added: M3 sits on the axis with its line across Grow retention, its two items tied to it; Undo in the top corner.
The same M3 on the Gantt, drawn the same way over the week columns.
“Add and place another”: M3 is saved, M4 waits dashed on Feb 17 and the card asks for its name.
Now / Next / Later after M3 is added: each horizon lists its milestones above its cards, with its own “+ Milestone”.
Hard case at 1512, Gantt with 30 items in Grow retention: M2 and Faster activation's M2 on the same day (one diamond, “2 on Dec 22”), M3 before an item it waits on, M4 after it.
Phone 390, Gantt: a tap on the axis opens the same card as a sheet from the bottom.
Phone 390: M3 added; every label keeps all its words: near an edge it sits on the inside or wraps to two lines.
The Timeline result in dark mode.
Phone 390 in dark mode.

proposals.why: It is the most direct answer to “create one directly on the timeline or Gantt”: one click on the day, then the same card everywhere, and it repeats for a ladder of milestones.

proposals.name: Pick items, then mark
proposals.what: The owner ticks the items a milestone waits on, then “Make a milestone after these” in a bar at the foot. The card opens with those items in it and the day after the last one ends.
proposals.plus: The items it waits on come first, so a milestone is never empty; the date is right by default.
proposals.cost: Two steps before anything shows on the chart; no way to make a milestone that waits on nothing yet; ticks on rows are new on both charts.

frames.caption: At rest: nothing new on the chart; a tip above the add bar says to tick items first.
Two items ticked (their bars outlined); a bar at the foot offers “Make a milestone after these”.
The card opens with the two picked items already in it; the owner names it and sets the day.
Added: M3 on the Timeline, tied to the two items picked.
The same M3 on the Gantt.
The next one: Weekly alert digest ticked, the card opens for M4 with it already in.
Hard case at 1512, Gantt with 30 items in Grow retention: the same two on Dec 22 and M3 before an item it waits on. Cost: among 30 rows, every item has to be found and ticked first.
Phone 390: ticks on the bars and a short bar at the foot, “Make a milestone”.
The Gantt result in dark mode. Cost: a milestone with no items yet cannot be made this way.

proposals.name: Type it in a bar
proposals.what: A second bar under “Add an item” takes a milestone in words (“M3 Teams set 3 rules by Jan 20”). A dashed preview shows where it lands; Enter adds it and the bar stays ready for the next one.
proposals.plus: Fastest for a list of milestones; works on any view, phone too.
proposals.cost: Not on the chart itself; dates must be typed; the items it waits on are added later; one more bar on a busy page.

frames.caption: At rest: a second add bar, “Add a milestone”, under the item add bar.
Typed “M3 Teams set 3 rules in week 1 by Jan 20”: a dashed preview shows where it lands before Enter.
Enter: M3 is drawn; the items it waits on still have to be added from its diamond.
The same M3 on the Gantt, with no items tied to it.
The bar stays ready for the next one: “M4 Digest opened by 70% by Feb 17” typed, M4 shown dashed on Feb 17. Cost: one more bar on the page.
Hard case at 1512, Gantt with 30 items in Grow retention: the same two on Dec 22; nothing says which items M3 waits on.
Phone 390: the add bar takes the words on a phone too.
The Gantt result in dark mode.

proposals.name: Drag from a chip
proposals.what: A “Drag a milestone onto a date” chip sits in the chart's corner. Dragging it shades the goal row under it and shows the day; dropping opens the card.
proposals.plus: Easy to find; the drop picks both the day and the goal.
proposals.cost: One drag per milestone; no room to drag on a phone, so a phone cannot add; drag code is the costliest to test.

frames.caption: At rest: a “Drag a milestone onto a date” chip in the chart's corner.
Dragging the chip: Grow retention's rows are shaded and a guide line shows the day it drops on, Jan 20.
Dropped on Jan 20: the same card as the others opens to name it and pick its items.
Added: M3 on Jan 20 on the Timeline.
The same M3 on the Gantt.
The next one: the chip dragged again, onto Feb 17, and the card opens for M4. Cost: one drag per milestone.
Hard case at 1512, Gantt with 30 items in Grow retention: the same two on Dec 22; with the chart scrolled, the drop day is harder to aim at.
Phone 390: no room to drag a chip, so a phone has no way to add with this one.
The Gantt result in dark mode.

decisions.name: What it asks and shows
decisions.question: What does a new milestone ask for, how is it drawn, and how is it moved, edited and removed?
decisions.common: A milestone has a name with its code (M3), a date, a goal, the items it waits on, a rule for when it counts and a status. A diamond on the time axis marks its day; a drag on the axis moves it; a click opens it; every change has Undo.

proposals.name: Card, line per goal
proposals.what: A small card in the chart's top corner asks for name, date, goal, the items it waits on (tapped on the chart) and when it counts. It is drawn as a diamond on the axis and a line across its own goal's rows only, with its items tied to it by dotted lines; an item that ends after it says “Ends after M3” in red. A drag on the diamond moves it, a click opens the card to edit or remove, with Undo.
proposals.plus: Each goal reads as its own ladder; late items show where they are; the card asks for everything in one place without leaving the chart.
proposals.cost: More lines on a busy chart; ties and late marks need drawing on both charts and on a phone.

frames.caption: At rest: each milestone a diamond on the axis, a line across its own goal's rows, named in the goal's row.
Add M3: the card asks for name, date, goal, the items it waits on (tapped on the chart) and when it counts.
M3 added: a diamond on the axis, a line across its own goal's rows only, its items tied by dotted lines, and “Ends after M3” on the late one.
Edit M3: a click on the new M3 opens its card again, with Remove.
Done: the same M3 on the Gantt.
A second in a row: M4 waits dashed on Feb 17 while its card asks for the rest.
Moving: the diamond dragged along the axis to Jan 27; a tip says what changes as it goes.
Removed: M3 is gone, with Undo in the top corner.
Hard case at 1512, 30 items in Grow retention: two milestones on Dec 22, and an item that ends after M3.
Phone 390: lines and ties kept; labels keep all their words, wrapping to two lines near an edge.
The Gantt result in dark mode.

proposals.name: Side panel, full line
proposals.what: A panel at the right asks for every field, the status, and the goal's items as a tick list. It is drawn as one line down the whole chart with its name at the top; late items are marked, with no ties.
proposals.plus: Room for long names and rules; the tick list is easy with 30 items.
proposals.cost: The panel hides part of the chart while picking; full-height lines cross other goals' rows and read as theirs; on a phone the sheet hides the chart.

frames.caption: At rest: each milestone a line down the whole chart, named at the top of the rows.
Add M3: the panel has every field and the status, and ticks the goal's items it waits on. Cost: it covers the right of the chart, where M3 sits.
M3 added: a line down the whole chart with its name at the top; no ties, the late item marked.
Edit M3: a click on the new M3 opens the side panel again, with Remove; the panel covers the right of the chart.
Done: the same on the Gantt, where every milestone crosses every goal's rows.
A second in a row: M4's line dashed on Feb 17, the panel open again for it.
Hard case at 1512, 30 items in Grow retention: two milestones on Dec 22, and an item that ends after M3; every line crosses all 30 rows.
Phone 390: the panel becomes a sheet; the chart is hidden under it.
The Gantt result in dark mode.

proposals.name: Name and date only
proposals.what: A small card asks for a name and a date only; the rest is added later from its diamond. It is drawn as a diamond on the axis and a small one in the goal's header row.
proposals.cost: Shows nothing about what it waits on or what is late, so the chart cannot warn; the rest is easy to forget.

frames.caption: At rest: a diamond on the axis, and the milestone named with a small diamond in its goal's row; no lines.
Add M3: a small card asks only for a name and a date.
M3 added: a diamond on the axis and its name in the goal's row; nothing on the items. The toast only says “M3 added”.
Edit M3: a click on the new M3 opens the small card again to edit its name and date, with Remove.
Done: the same on the Gantt; least clutter, but no sign of what it waits on or what is late.
A second in a row: M4 named in the row on Feb 17, the small card open for it.
Hard case at 1512, 30 items in Grow retention: two milestones on Dec 22; the item that ends after M3 is not marked.
Phone 390: the names in the goal rows, nothing on the items.
The Gantt result in dark mode.

decisions.name: A PRD's own milestones
decisions.question: How do a PRD's own milestones show on the roadmap, and what happens when one is changed there?
decisions.common: A roadmap built from a PRD draws the PRD's milestones on its goal (today it shows none). They are drawn hollow and marked as the PRD's, apart from the roadmap's own.

proposals.name: Edit asks the PRD
proposals.what: The PRD's milestones are drawn hollow with dashed lines and a “PRD” tag. They can be dragged or edited like the roadmap's own, but the change is sent to the PRD's owner as a change to approve; until then the asked-for day shows dashed amber beside the real one. No “second in a row” here: MS3 is about changing a PRD's milestone, not adding one.
proposals.plus: One place to plan; the PRD stays the source and its owner decides; the owner never leaves Simple.
proposals.cost: A waiting change has two places on the chart for a while; needs the PRD change flow to accept milestone changes.

frames.caption: A roadmap built with the PRD Usage alerts: its four milestones drawn hollow with dashed lines, each label starting “PRD”, and a key above the chart.
Opened: it says it comes from the PRD and who owns it; a change here is sent to her to approve.
M2 Digest for all teams dragged to Jan 5: the old place fades; the new place is a dashed M2 diamond with an amber “Moving” tag.
Asked: the PRD's M2 stays put until Nora Vance says yes; the asked-for day waits beside it.
The same waiting change on the Gantt.
Hard case at 1512, 30 items in Grow retention: the PRD's four milestones named over the long goal.
Phone 390: the PRD milestone opens as a sheet from the bottom.
The asked change in dark mode.

proposals.name: Locked, link to PRD
proposals.what: The PRD's milestones are drawn hollow with a lock. Opening one is read only, with “Open it in the PRD”; a drag is refused on the spot with the same link. No result or “second in a row” frames: a drag is refused and nothing changes.
proposals.plus: Simple to build; the PRD is plainly the only place to change it.
proposals.cost: The owner has to leave the roadmap to move a date; the chart feels stuck.

frames.caption: The PRD's four milestones drawn hollow, each label with a lock; the key says they change only in the PRD.
Opened: read only, with “Open it in the PRD”.
A drag is refused on the spot, with a link to the PRD. Nothing changes, so there is no result to show.
Hard case at 1512, 30 items in Grow retention: the PRD's four locked milestones over the long goal.
Phone 390: the read-only sheet.
At rest in dark mode.

proposals.name: Copy onto roadmap
proposals.what: The PRD's milestones are not drawn; a line on the axis says the PRD has 4 and offers to copy them. Copies belong to the roadmap and move freely. No “second in a row”: one copy brings all four over.
proposals.plus: Full freedom on the roadmap; nothing to approve.
proposals.cost: Copies drift from the PRD with no warning; two sets of the same milestones to keep straight.

frames.caption: Not drawn: one line above the chart says the PRD has 4 milestones, with “Copy onto the roadmap”.
The copy list: tick which to bring over.
Copied: they now belong to the roadmap and move freely; the PRD stays as it is, and the two can drift apart.
The copies on the Gantt.
Hard case at 1512, 30 items in Grow retention: nothing of the PRD is drawn until it is copied, only the line above the chart.
Phone 390: the copies; on a phone the copy line is not shown, so copying waits for a desktop.
The copies in dark mode.
